messages:
marta: Quick follow-up on the holdback-throttle + autoswitch behavior after the RFC — we saw flip-flop during the last canary and I want to lock down the runtime contract for holdback windows so autoswitch doesn't oscillate under token surges. Thoughts?

arjun: +1. My high-level idea: decision service should emit a short-lived score that decays on a wall-clock timer (seconds) instead of per-request. On spikes we increment the score; only cross a threshold once. That gives us time-based hysteresis and avoids request-count jitter.

camille: Can we define the wire contract? Ops wants deterministic signals to attach to traces. Something like: {action, min_hold_s, cooldown_s, reason}. Simple, opaque.

samir: concrete thresholds I saw working in testing: failure_rate > 4% sustained for 25s AND p95 latency > 1.8s -> mark fallback. Also require an absolute minimum stable window of 120s before another switch for the same tenant.

liz: Ops note: tenant-level oscillation is the main risk. Two suggestions: 1) require cross-az confirmation for global autoswitch (so transient AZ blips don't flip everyone), 2) persist decision to observer/state-store so a controller restart doesn't immediately undo it.

marta: Good. Also: make autoswitch idempotent from the caller side — caller can retry the decision call and get the same answer until the min_hold expires. We should avoid ephemeral contradictions between router and observer.

arjun: interface sketch (proto-ish) for decision service:```json
{
  "action": "redirect|mirror|keep",
  "min_hold_s": 120,
  "cooldown_s": 300,
  "score": 0.78,
  "reason": "p95_latency_and_error_rate"
}
```This keeps it simple and debuggable in traces.

camille: +emoji :thumbsup: — also add a small human-readable tag for tooling (e.g., "probe=latency-p95-1.8s").

deploy-bot: note: canary v2 -> v3 at 10:23 UTC had a 6% error spike for ~40s; an autoswitch fired then recovered in ~30s leading to two switches inside a 90s window. Logged as deploy/37891.

liz: That exactly matches the fail-case. If decision cooldown is too short, we create noisy rollbacks. I propose we: a) min_hold = 120s, b) cooldown = 300s, c) require at least 2 distinct probes (AZs or observer partitions) to agree for global actions.

samir: implementation caveat: for Dedicated customers we might allow softer thresholds per-tenant (configurable) but default to conservative values. Also ensure the router exposes a "switch-score" header for telemetry so we can graph pre/post behavior.

marta: Operational checklist before we flip this into RFC: 1) add persisted state for active holds (observer-backed) 2) decision API as above + traceable reason tag 3) unit + integration tests that simulate AZ flaps 4) migration plan for existing canaries (a toggle to opt-in).

arjun: I'll draft a small follow-up RFC with the proto, sample headers, and a reference impl for the observer-backed store. Will include test scenarios.

camille: please include example curl + header snippets for SRE runbook.

marta: Thanks — if anyone has objections speak now, otherwise i'll mark this as an RFC follow-up item and @arjun will own the draft. :white_check_mark:
